questions.stem: A client taking dabigatran has life-threatening, uncontrolled bleeding. Which specific reversal agent should the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Idarucizumab (Praxbind) is a specific reversal agent for dabigatran and is indicated when reversal of dabigatran's anticoagulant effect is needed for emergency surgery/urgent procedures or life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding. Protamine reverses heparin, vitamin K reverses vitamin K antagonists, and naloxone reverses opioids.
questions.source_detail: Indications and Usage: reversal of dabigatran anticoagulant effects for emergency surgery/urgent procedures or life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding.

questions.stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is prescribed apixaban. Which statement about the labeled adult dose-reduction criteria is accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The standard dose is reduced when at least two of these are present: age 80 years or older, body weight 60 kg or less, or serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or greater.","B":"Any degree of renal impairment automatically requires the lowest apixaban dose.","C":"Renal function, age, and body weight never affect apixaban dosing.","D":"The apixaban dose is doubled whenever serum creatinine exceeds 1.5 mg/dL."}}
questions.rationale: For stroke and systemic embolism prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, the current ELIQUIS label recommends 5 mg twice daily for most adults and 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria are present: age at least 80 years, body weight at most 60 kg, or serum creatinine at least 1.5 mg/dL. The prior item was too broad because apixaban dosing is indication-specific and renal impairment alone is not the universal rule described there.
questions.source_detail: Current label version 38, section 2.1: NVAF dose 5 mg twice daily; reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL are present.

questions.stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. When is initiation most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"After the client is clinically stabilized, before discharge when appropriate, rather than during ongoing hemodynamic instability.","B":"Immediately at a full target dose while the client remains in marked low-output instability.","C":"Never, because beta-blockers are permanently contraindicated in all clients with HFrEF.","D":"Only after all other guideline-directed heart-failure therapies have been permanently discontinued."}}
questions.rationale: Guideline-directed beta-blockers are foundational therapy for HFrEF. In hospitalized patients, initiation is appropriate after clinical stabilization and before discharge when feasible. Existing beta-blocker therapy is generally continued unless clinical circumstances such as marked volume overload, marginal low output, or other intolerance require adjustment. The prior wording incorrectly implied that beta-blockers are broadly avoided throughout acute decompensation.
questions.source_name: AHA/ACC/HFSA — 2022 Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
questions.source_detail: Hospitalized HFrEF guidance: initiate guideline-directed therapy after clinical stability is achieved; beta-blocker initiation before discharge is reasonable once stabilized, while dose reduction/withholding may be considered with marked volume overload or marginal low output.

questions.stem: A client has severe digoxin toxicity with a life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. Which treatment should the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Digoxin immune Fab binds digoxin and is indicated for life-threatening or potentially life-threatening digoxin toxicity, including serious ventricular arrhythmias. The other agents reverse different drug classes.
questions.source_name: DailyMed — DIGIFAB (digoxin immune Fab) prescribing information
questions.source_detail: Indications and Usage: treatment of life-threatening or potentially life-threatening digoxin toxicity, including severe ventricular arrhythmias and other specified manifestations.

questions.stem: An adult client is prescribed insulin degludec (TRESIBA) once daily and asks whether every dose must be given at exactly the same clock time. Which teaching is correct?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"For adults, TRESIBA is labeled for once-daily injection at any time of day; dosing should still follow the prescribed plan and missed-dose instructions.","B":"Adults must administer TRESIBA at exactly the same minute every day or the dose becomes unsafe.","C":"TRESIBA is a rapid-acting mealtime insulin and should be given before every meal.","D":"The flexible adult timing instruction also means pediatric patients should routinely vary the time each day."}}
questions.rationale: The current TRESIBA label states that adults inject once daily at any time of day, while pediatric patients should inject once daily at the same time every day. Adult timing flexibility therefore should not be generalized to pediatric dosing.
questions.source_detail: Section 2.2 General Dosing Instructions: adults inject once daily at any time of day; pediatric patients inject once daily at the same time every day.

questions.stem: Before giving sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain, the nurse learns that the client recently used sildenafil. Why is this important?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Nitroglycerin is contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil because the combination can cause severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia.","B":"Sildenafil prevents nitroglycerin absorption but has no hemodynamic interaction.","C":"The combination is recommended because it safely enhances coronary vasodilation.","D":"There is no established interaction between nitrates and sildenafil."}}
questions.rationale: Current nitroglycerin labeling contraindicates use in patients taking PDE-5 inhibitors including sildenafil because concomitant use can cause severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia.
questions.source_name: DailyMed — Nitroglycerin Sublingual Tablets prescribing information
questions.source_detail: Section 4.1 PDE-5 Inhibitors and sGC Stimulators: do not use with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or avanafil; severe hypotension, syncope, or myocardial ischemia can occur.

questions.stem: During central venous catheter insertion, why should the nurse use a standardized insertion checklist that includes hand hygiene, maximal sterile barrier precautions, and appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"To promote consistent adherence to evidence-based measures that reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection risk.","B":"To replace sterile technique when the operator is experienced.","C":"To eliminate the need to assess whether the central line remains necessary after insertion.","D":"To permit skipping individual infection-prevention steps when venous access appears easy."}}
questions.rationale: CDC central-line prevention recommendations include hand hygiene, maximal sterile barrier precautions for insertion, chlorhexidine-based skin preparation, and appropriate catheter-site practices. A checklist supports reliable implementation but does not replace sterile technique or ongoing review of line necessity.
questions.source_name: CDC — Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections
questions.source_detail: Summary recommendations: hand hygiene; maximal sterile barrier precautions during CVC insertion; chlorhexidine skin preparation; prompt removal of catheters no longer essential.

questions.stem: A reusable surgical instrument is heavily soiled with blood and tissue during a procedure. Which point-of-use practice best supports effective later reprocessing?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Follow the manufacturer's point-of-use instructions and prevent gross soil from drying before transport for full cleaning and sterilization.","B":"Allow blood and tissue to dry completely because dried soil improves sterilant penetration.","C":"Skip cleaning if terminal sterilization will be performed later.","D":"Use any unvalidated chemical available, regardless of the device manufacturer's instructions."}}
questions.rationale: Effective sterilization depends on adequate cleaning. CDC guidance states that devices should be cleaned as soon as practical after use because dried soil makes removal more difficult and can interfere with disinfection or sterilization. Point-of-use handling should follow validated manufacturer instructions rather than improvised chemicals.
questions.source_name: CDC — Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities
questions.source_detail: Cleaning section: clean medical devices as soon as practical after use because materials become dried onto instruments; cleaning is required before high-level disinfection and sterilization.

questions.stem: A nurse on a burn unit asks whether every patient with a serious burn automatically requires a special universal 'burn isolation' protocol beyond Standard and indicated Transmission-Based Precautions. Which response is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"No. Infection prevention is critical, but CDC notes there is no single proven universal barrier-isolation regimen for all serious burn patients; hand hygiene and precautions should follow patient-specific risks and facility policy.","B":"Yes. Every burn patient must be placed in airborne isolation regardless of infection status.","C":"No infection-prevention measures are needed because burn wounds are not susceptible to colonization or infection.","D":"Every burn patient must be managed in a HEPA-filtered positive-pressure room regardless of transplant status or infection risk."}}
questions.rationale: Serious burns disrupt skin integrity and infection prevention is important, but the prior item overstated a universal 'stricter isolation' approach. CDC's scientific review states that there is no consensus on the most effective special infection-control configuration for serious burn patients and no defined universal combination of barrier precautions. Standard Precautions and indicated Transmission-Based Precautions remain fundamental, with additional burn-unit practices based on risk and facility policy.
questions.source_name: CDC — Isolation Precautions Scientific Review: Burn Patients
questions.source_detail: Scientific review section on patients with serious burns: no consensus on the most effective special infection-control practices or barrier-precaution combination; evidence supports emphasis on hand hygiene and appropriate barriers for direct contact.

questions.stem: An allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipient is placed in a CDC-defined Protective Environment. What is the primary purpose of this environment?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"To reduce the recipient's exposure to environmental fungal spores through specified engineering controls while Standard and indicated Transmission-Based Precautions continue.","B":"To protect staff from the transplant recipient by replacing Standard Precautions.","C":"To eliminate the need for hand hygiene and personal protective equipment.","D":"To place every immunocompromised patient in the same room configuration regardless of transplant type."}}
questions.rationale: CDC's Protective Environment is specifically recommended for allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant patients to reduce exposure to environmental fungi using engineering controls such as HEPA filtration and positive pressure. It does not replace Standard or Transmission-Based Precautions and should not be generalized to every immunocompromised patient.
questions.source_name: CDC — Guideline for Isolation Precautions, Protective Environment
questions.source_detail: Protective Environment recommendations: use for allogeneic HSCT patients to reduce environmental fungal exposure; maintain Standard and Transmission-Based Precautions as indicated.
